name: Single Leg for BJJ
description: Finish the single leg while respecting guillotine, kimura, and guard pull threats in BJJ. The single leg in BJJ must be adapted from wrestling to account for the unique counters that exist in submission grappling.
shortInstruction: Secure the leg, keep your head to the outside (not the center), and finish by running the pipe, lifting, or circling to the back. Never let your head drift to the inside where they can guillotine you.
summary: The BJJ single leg is a modified version of the wrestling single leg that prioritizes safety from submission counters. The key adaptations are: head position must always be to the outside (cheek to their hip/back) rather than the inside (chest to their chest), the finish prioritizes running the pipe (driving them laterally) over lifting (which exposes the guillotine), and the back take is always available as a high-percentage alternative to the takedown finish.
whyItWorks: Outside head position prevents the guillotine — the most common counter to single legs in BJJ
Running the pipe (lateral drive) keeps your head safe and uses their weight against them
The back take from the single leg is a BJJ-specific adaptation that scores 4 points instead of 2
The single leg transitions to both top position and back control — it is the most versatile takedown in BJJ
commonMistakes: Letting your head drift inside (chest to chest) — this exposes you to the guillotine, kimura, and front headlock
Trying to lift the leg straight up — this delays the finish and exposes the guillotine
Staying too long on the leg — the single leg must be finished quickly or abandoned
Not transitioning to the back when the finish is blocked
safetySummary: The guillotine from a failed single leg is the most common choke in BJJ — keep your head to the outside at all times
If you feel the guillotine setting up, immediately circle to the back rather than trying to finish the takedown
Do not hold the single leg and stand straight — this exposes the knee to reaps and the neck to guillotines
keyCorrections: If they guillotine you: your head was inside — circle to the back immediately to relieve the choke pressure
If they kimura your trapped arm: do not fight the kimura — release the leg and re-engage from standing
If they hop away on one leg: switch to a high crotch or dump them laterally with the running pipe

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The BJJ single leg has four finishes: Running Pipe → Lift → Back Take → High Crotch Dump

decisionTree.action: with the leg trapped and head outside, drive them laterally across the mat. Their far leg cannot keep up with the lateral movement and they fall. Safest finish in BJJ
if they are off-balance (weight on one leg), lift the trapped leg and drive them backward. Only use this if head position is confirmed outside
if they sprawl on the single leg, release the leg and circle behind them. The back take scores 4 points and avoids the sprawl counter
if they post the far leg back, switch to a high crotch grip and dump them to the opposite side
if they guillotine → back take. If they kimura → release and re-engage. If they sprawl → back take

moneyDetails: The single leg is the most common takedown in BJJ — a reliable finish is essential for competitive success
Mastering the BJJ-adapted single leg removes the fear of takedown counters and allows you to shoot with confidence
The single leg to back take is the highest-value sequence in no-gi takedowns (4 points instead of 2)
fixItFast: If they sprawl on the single leg: go to the back take — do not fight the sprawl
If they guillotine: circle to the back immediately — the back take defeats the guillotine
If they hop on one leg: drive them laterally with the running pipe — they cannot hop sideways
